# SingleStoreDB

[https://www.singlestore.com](https://www.singlestore.com)

![](https://img.shields.io/badge/memtables-fallback-yellow?style=flat-square) ![](https://img.shields.io/badge/inputs-SingleStoreDB tables-blue?style=flat-square) ![](https://img.shields.io/badge/outputs-SingleStoreDB tables | CSV | pandas | Parquet | PyArrow-orange?style=flat-square)

## Install

Install Ibis and dependencies for the SingleStoreDB backend:

::: {.panel-tabset}

## `pip`

Install with the `singlestoredb` extra:

```{.bash}
pip install 'ibis-framework[singlestoredb]'
```

And connect:

```{.python}
import ibis

con = ibis.singlestoredb.connect()  # <1>
```

1. Adjust connection parameters as needed.

## `conda`

Install for SingleStoreDB:

```{.bash}
conda install -c conda-forge ibis-singlestoredb
```

And connect:

```{.python}
import ibis

con = ibis.singlestoredb.connect()  # <1>
```

1. Adjust connection parameters as needed.

## `mamba`

Install for SingleStoreDB:

```{.bash}
mamba install -c conda-forge ibis-singlestoredb
```

And connect:

```{.python}
import ibis

con = ibis.singlestoredb.connect()  # <1>
```

1. Adjust connection parameters as needed.

:::

## Connect

### `ibis.singlestoredb.connect`

```python
con = ibis.singlestoredb.connect(
    user="username",
    password="password",
    host="hostname",
    port=3306,
    database="database",
)
```

::: {.callout-note}
`ibis.singlestoredb.connect` is a thin wrapper around [`ibis.backends.singlestoredb.Backend.do_connect`](#ibis.backends.singlestoredb.Backend.do_connect).
:::

### Connection Parameters

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _utils import render_do_connect

render_do_connect("singlestoredb")
```

### `ibis.connect` URL format

In addition to `ibis.singlestoredb.connect`, you can also connect to SingleStoreDB by
passing a properly-formatted SingleStoreDB connection URL to `ibis.connect`:

```python
con = ibis.connect(f"singlestoredb://{user}:{password}@{host}:{port}/{database}")
```

## JSON objects and arrays

Use `.map` and `.array` on JSON columns to work with JSON objects and arrays.
Both give NULL when the value has a different JSON type:

```python
t = con.table("docs")
t.select(
    keys=t.metadata.map.keys(),
    nested_keys=t.metadata["address"].map.keys(),
    has_city=t.metadata["address"].map.contains("city"),
    num_tags=t.metadata["tags"].array.length(),
    first_tag=t.metadata["tags"].array[0],
    has_red=t.metadata["tags"].array.contains("red"),
)
```

`VECTOR` columns are read as fixed-length arrays and support the same array
methods, `length`, indexing and `contains`, through the JSON functions.

## SingleStoreDB vector and JSON functions

`ibis.backends.singlestoredb.functions` has SingleStoreDB's vector and JSON
functions that have no Ibis method, in its `vector` and `json` modules. They
build expressions and don't need a connection:

```python
from ibis.backends.singlestoredb import functions as s2

t.select(
    score=s2.vector.dot_product(t.embedding, [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]),
    kind=s2.json.get_type(t.metadata["tags"]),
    city=s2.json.extract_string(t.metadata, "address", "city"),
    has_big_score=s2.json.match_any(
        lambda v: v > 90, t.metadata, "scores", value_type="bigint"
    ),
)
```

Each function's documentation names the SQL function it calls, such as
`JSON_EXTRACT_STRING` for `json.extract_string`. Import the package as shown
rather than `from ... import json`, which would hide Python's `json` module.

Vector arguments can be `VECTOR` columns, JSON arrays, Python sequences, or
`BLOB` columns of packed vectors. The element type comes from a `VECTOR`
argument or the element type of an array, so you don't need to pass it,
except for packed `BLOB` vectors whose elements aren't 32-bit floats:

```python
s2.vector.dot_product(t.packed_i8, [1, 2, 3], element_type="i8")
```

Functions that return a vector return a `VECTOR` if any argument is one, and
a packed `BLOB` otherwise. `vector.from_json` packs a JSON array into a
`BLOB` vector, and `vector.to_json` unpacks one into a JSON array.

## User-defined functions

`con.function` returns a callable for a user-defined function or aggregate
on the server. It looks up the signature on each call, so assign the result
to reuse it:

```python
my_add = con.function("my_add")
my_mul = con.function("my_mul", database="other_db")
t.select(total=my_add(t.x, t.y), product=my_mul(t.x, t.y))
```

For other builtins that have no Ibis method, declare a
[builtin UDF](../how-to/extending/builtin.qmd):

```python
@ibis.udf.scalar.builtin(name="SIGMOID")
def sigmoid(x: float) -> float: ...


t.select(p=sigmoid(t.score))
```

## Server variables

`ibis.backends.singlestoredb.server` has functions that take a connection
for server variables and `SHOW` commands:

```python
from ibis.backends.singlestoredb import server

server.globals(con)["max_connections"]
server.locals(con)["autocommit"] = False
server.show(con).tables()
```

The variable accessors are `globals`, `locals`, `vars`, `cluster_globals`,
`cluster_locals` and `cluster_vars`.

```{python}
#| echo: false
BACKEND = "SingleStoreDB"
```
